learningObjective: Distinguish dynamic (request-level) batching from continuous (iteration-level) batching and diagnose a workload that suffers head-of-line blocking.

canonicalClaims.claim: Static (request-level) batching suffers head-of-line blocking with variable output lengths: the batch holds until the longest request finishes, wasting SM parallelism on nearly-empty batches. Continuous (iteration-level) batching removes this by rebatching per iteration.
conditions: Output length variance is significant across the batch.
Scheduler decides batch composition per model-forward iteration.
nonImplications: Does not imply continuous batching solves all imbalance.
Does not require any particular KV cache layout (paged or contiguous).

misconceptions.claim: KV cache quantization solves head-of-line blocking.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Quantization addresses bandwidth, not batch composition.
CUDA Graphs amortize launch overhead but the batch composition remains static.
Spec decoding accelerates per-request decode but does not let other requests leave the batch.

implementationFacts: Continuous batching is core to vLLM, SGLang, and TRT-LLM's inflight batching.
It composes with chunked prefill to interleave prefill and decode without long stalls.
performanceScenarios: Chat workloads with mixed short/long outputs benefit most from iteration-level batching.
